checked.label: hope-lifetime 97%
problems: Ethnic-group sentence and its alsoRef moved to notUsed.numbers[21]; nothing dropped without an entry. 'A projected 66% within 10 years' matches '66.2% for cannabis' a decade after onset.

checked.label: who-age Age 29
problems: basis.measured: 'the time from first use to the end of the problem at about 12 years' sits right after 'first used weed at 15', so a reader computes 29-15=14 and sees a mismatch. The paper defines the 11.74-year 'addiction career' as 'the number of years from age of first use for any substance to the age at which they resolved', i.e. first use of any drug or drink, not of weed. Say so.

fix.numbers[3].basis.measured: Age when the problem ended, as people remembered it. On average they first used weed at 15 and weekly at about 17. The paper puts the time from first use of any drug or drink to the end of the problem at about 12 years.

checked.label: how-abrupt 85 in 100
problems: counted reads 'not checked for addiction; 3 in 4 met a self-report problem checklist', which contradicts itself (they were checked, by a self-report DSM-5 checklist, mild cases included: 'Most (75%) met criteria for DSM- 5 Cannabis Use Disorder using a self-report version of the DSM checklist'). Keep the heavy-tag wording but say what kind of check was missing, and that mild cases count.

fix.numbers[6].counted: daily weed users, not checked for addiction by a doctor; 3 in 4 met a self-report problem checklist, mild cases included

checked.label: helps-medicine 27 vs 26 in 100
problems: Arm figures match the Summary of findings ('262 per 1000', '270 per 1000 (184 to 396)', 290 people, 4 RCTs); NAC 352 vs 411 per 1000 (2 RCTs, 270) gives 35 vs 41 in 100; 'diagnosed as cannabis dependent or who are likely to be dependent' backs the treatment tag; 'should still be considered experimental' backs the caveat. Headline 2 figures, 21 words, not more hopeful.

checked.label: how-with-help 23 in 100
problems: Figures match ('an average of 37% ... at end of treatment ... and to 23% at follow-up of longer than four months. In contrast, an average of 12% of those in control conditions reported PPA at final follow-up'; RR 2.55, six studies, 1166; 'at least near daily cannabis users'; 'five out of six studies supported ... voucher-based incentives ... on cannabis use frequency'). Kind how-with-help exists in kinds.json (group how, treatment reader).

Rule 25: two sentences cut from the rev2 basis.measured have no notUsed entry: 'little or none means minimal or no treatment, such as waiting for treatment later' and 'The review sums up the treated as about a quarter off weed at the last check-up' (source: 'approximately one-quarter of participants abstinent at final follow-up'). The first defines 'little or no treatment', which the card still uses; put it back. Log the second in notUsed.

fix.numbers[8].basis.measured: Off weed means no use in the month before the check-up, as people reported it; about half of all the trials checked reports with urine tests or people close to them. The 23 in 100 is the average in the 8 trials that counted this, at check-ups more than 4 months on (37 in 100 at the end of treatment). Groups given little or no treatment (such as waiting for treatment later) averaged 12 in 100 at their last check-up, but the review does not say from which trials or at what time, so the two are not a fair comparison. Therapy was about 7 sessions over 12 weeks.

notUsed.numbers[+].text: The review sums up the treated as about a quarter off weed at the last check-up.
notUsed.numbers[+].why: Repeats the 23 in 100 in other words; cut so the card holds one figure for one idea (rev3).

checked.label: how-withdrawal Day 2-6
problems: Abstract quote word for word; Hesse 2013 alsoRef quote word for word (PMC4015312). Note: Bonnet 2017's table describes the 18 as 'frequent, heavy cannabis users seeking treatment'; the card does not claim otherwise and the heavy tag is the cautious one, so no change.

checked.label: how-withdrawal 28 in 100 (owner liked 47%)
problems: 47 in 100 is accurate for its group as worded. It is the review's own headline result, in the Key Points ('the prevalence of cannabis withdrawal syndrome was found to be 47%') and the abstract ('The overall pooled prevalence of CWS was 47% (6469 of 23 518) (95% CI, 41%-52%)'), for 'people with regular or dependent use'. It is the pooled average of 50 cohorts' own rates; arithmetic on the subgroups confirms it: (15x17 + 28x54 + 7x87)/50 = 47.5.

The 28 in 100 head count (6,469 of 23,518) is not the more accurate figure for this reader. 17,475 of the 23,518 people come from the 15 general-population surveys, where withdrawal was 17% and only 8% to 34% had a disorder. So the head count mostly reflects survey users, not hooked men. Rule 10 (cautious first) covers projections and hope figures; a higher withdrawal share is not more hopeful, it is the 'it's not just you' answer the mirror needs.
Owner liked '47%' in v10 (rule 26; kinds.json how-withdrawal 'why': 'weed: day 2–6, 47%'). Restore it as the big figure in the page's 'in 100' format.
The headline must not say '47 studies' next to '47 in 100' (rev2 cold readers read it as a typo), and must say it is an average of studies, not a head count.

Paper flaw to know (not for the card): the results text gives '47% (95% CI, 27%-37%)', a range that does not contain 47; the abstract's 41%-52% fits. The 47% itself appears consistently in Key Points, abstract and results.

fix.numbers[10].headline: On average across dozens of studies, about 47 in 100 regular or hooked weed users got withdrawal when they stopped.
fix.numbers[10].basis.measured: Share who met the criteria for weed withdrawal on a tested checklist. The 47 in 100 is the review's pooled average of the studies' own rates. Counting every person instead, 6,469 of 23,518 had it (about 28 in 100), because the biggest studies were general surveys, where rates were lowest.
fix.numbers[10].propose: It mixes regular users with people who were hooked (rule 2); a hooked reader is closer to the 54 in 100 for outpatients in the caveat.

checked.label: how-slips 71 in 100
problems: Quote word for word. Severity dependent: the abstract says only 'outpatient treatment for marijuana dependence' (the 'marijuana-dependent outpatients' phrase refers to earlier studies). It supports dependent as the programme's group, but it does not state that each of the 82 was diagnosed. Acceptable; 'treatment' would be the strictly safe tag if a later reviewer objects.
